local.body: Open the link shown in the terminal where KubeViz was started.
local.hint: The link carries an access token generated on each run, so other people on this machine cannot use your kubeconfig credentials.

token.label: Kubernetes access token
token.help: Use a ServiceAccount or user token. To create one:

password.tooMany: Too many attempts. Try again in {{minutes}} min.
password.hint: No account? Ask a KubeViz administrator.

oidc.hint: You will be taken to your organization's identity provider and brought back here.

errors.oidc_denied: Sign-in was cancelled or denied by the identity provider.
errors.oidc_state: Sign-in expired or was started in another tab. Please try again.
errors.oidc_claims: The identity provider did not return a valid user (a verified email or the configured claim). Contact your administrator.
errors.oidc_cluster: The cluster rejected your sign-in: the API server does not trust this identity provider. Contact your administrator.
errors.oidc_impersonate: KubeViz is not allowed to act on behalf of users (impersonate) in this cluster. Contact your administrator.
errors.oidc_unavailable: The identity provider is unreachable. Please try again shortly.
errors.oidc_failed: Sign-in could not be completed. Please try again.
errors.provider_denied: Sign-in was cancelled or denied by the provider.
errors.provider_state: Sign-in expired or was started in another tab. Please try again.
errors.provider_email: The provider did not confirm a verified email for your account.
errors.provider_unauthorized: This email does not have access to KubeViz yet. Ask an administrator to create your account.
errors.provider_unavailable: The sign-in provider is unreachable. Please try again shortly.
errors.provider_failed: Sign-in could not be completed. Please try again.

setup.title: Set up KubeViz
setup.intro: First access: create the administrator account. Then, under Administration, you can add other people and sign-in with Google, Microsoft or GitHub.
setup.usernameHelp: Lowercase letters, digits, dot, hyphen or underscore.
setup.after: For security, when KubeViz is reachable over the network, this account must be created within 15 minutes of starting it.
setup.taken: Someone else just created the administrator account. Ask them for access.
setup.expired: The time to create the administrator account is over (15 minutes after start). Restart KubeViz and open this page right away.

resources.forbiddenHint: Pick a namespace you have access to.
resources.notInstalled: {{what}} is not installed in this cluster
resources.notInstalledHint: This resource type comes from an extension (CRD) the cluster doesn't have.

live.liveHint: Updated in real time (Kubernetes API watch).
live.connectingHint: Opening the real-time connection; retrying if it drops.
live.pollingHint: No watch permission: the list is fetched every 10 seconds.

detail.notFoundHint: It may have been deleted or live in another namespace.
detail.name: Name
detail.secretHidden: Values are hidden. To see them, use the YAML tab.
detail.noEvents: No recent events for this object.

edit.validOk: Valid. The cluster would apply these changes:
edit.noChanges: Valid, but there's nothing to change.
edit.changedSinceValidation: The text changed after validation. Validate again to apply.
edit.conflict: Conflict: another manager owns these fields
edit.conflictHint: Forcing transfers ownership of these fields to KubeViz. The previous manager (a controller or kubectl) may try to revert the change.
edit.forbidden: Not allowed to change this object
edit.secretVisible: When editing a Secret, its values (base64) are visible in the editor.

applyYaml.subtitle: Paste or import one or more objects in YAML. The cluster validates before applying.
applyYaml.namespaceHint: used for objects without a namespace
applyYaml.missingName: {{kind}} without metadata.name (server-side apply doesn't accept generateName)
applyYaml.unknownKind: the cluster doesn't know the type {{type}} (is the extension/CRD installed?)
applyYaml.defaultedNamespace: No namespace in the YAML: it will be created in "{{ns}}".
applyYaml.droppedNamespace: This type has no namespace; the YAML namespace was ignored.
applyYaml.waitingHint: This object's namespace is created by this same YAML; full validation happens when applying.
applyYaml.summaryWaiting_one: {{count}} waits for a namespace in this batch.
applyYaml.summaryWaiting_other: {{count}} wait for a namespace in this batch.

logs.noPrevious: There's no previous run of this container (it hasn't restarted).

terminal.audit: Every terminal session is recorded in the KubeViz log. The cluster's RBAC must allow pods/exec.
terminal.notRunning: The pod isn't running; a terminal can't be opened.
terminal.refused: connection refused: check the pods/exec permission and that the shell exists in the image
terminal.noShell: the shell {{shell}} doesn't exist in this image; try sh or automatic

actions.scaleZero: With 0 replicas, all pods will be stopped.
actions.restartHint: Pods will be recreated gradually, following the update strategy (same as kubectl rollout restart).
actions.pauseHint: Template changes stop creating new versions until resumed. Current pods keep running.
actions.resumeHint: Pending template changes start being applied.
actions.rollbackTitle: Roll {{name}} back to a previous revision
actions.rollbackHint: The chosen revision's template takes effect again (same as kubectl rollout undo).
actions.noRevisions: There are no previous revisions to roll back to.
actions.cordonHint: New pods won't be scheduled on this node. Current pods keep running (same as kubectl cordon).
actions.uncordonHint: The node accepts new pods again (same as kubectl uncordon).
actions.deleteHint: This can't be undone. Dependent objects (like a ReplicaSet's pods) will also be deleted.

crds.subtitle: Resource types added to the cluster by extensions. Click a type to see its objects.
crds.unknownType: The cluster doesn't know the type {{type}}.

search.title: Global search
search.placeholder: Pages, resource types or object names…
search.hint: ↑↓ to navigate · Enter to open · Esc to close

users.subtitle: Who can sign in to KubeViz. In this installation (local mode), every account uses the machine's kubeconfig credentials.
users.dialogHint: The account signs in with a password, with one of the emails below (through the configured Google, Microsoft, GitHub or OIDC), or both.
users.removeHint: They are signed out immediately and can no longer sign in.
users.removeSelf: This is your account: you will be signed out immediately.
users.keepPassword: Leave empty to keep the current password.
users.passwordOptional: Optional if the account signs in by email only. At least 12 characters.
users.removePassword: Remove the password (the account signs in through a provider only)
users.emails: Emails to sign in with a provider
users.emailsHelp: One per line. The person clicks "Continue with Google" (or another) and gets in if the provider confirms this email.

domains.title: Allowed domains
domains.hint: Anyone signing in through a provider with an email from these domains gets an account (not administrator) on first access, without you creating it. One per line, e.g. company.com.

providers.subtitle: Allow signing in with Google, Microsoft, GitHub or another OIDC provider accounts. Only people with an account for the email confirmed by the provider (or from an allowed domain) get in.
providers.ipWarning: You are accessing KubeViz by IP address, which Google and Microsoft do not accept as a sign-in redirect. Use a name instead, for example {{url}}, and configure the providers from it.
providers.callback: Redirect URL (paste it in the provider)
providers.name: Button name
providers.tenantHelp: common: personal and work accounts; organizations: work only; consumers: personal only; or your organization's ID (GUID).

google.1: In the Google Cloud Console, set up the consent screen and create credentials › OAuth client ID › Web application.
google.2: Under "Authorized redirect URIs", paste the redirect URL below.
google.3: Copy the client ID and secret into the fields below and save.

microsoft.1: In Microsoft Entra, register an application (for personal and work accounts, choose "any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts").
microsoft.2: Under Authentication, add the Web platform with the redirect URL below; under Certificates & secrets, create a client secret.
microsoft.3: Copy the application (client) ID and the secret value into the fields below and save.

github.1: On GitHub, create an OAuth App (Settings › Developer settings).
github.2: Under "Authorization callback URL", paste the redirect URL below; then generate a client secret.
github.3: Copy the Client ID and secret into the fields below and save.

steps.oidc: Register KubeViz as a confidential client in the provider (Keycloak, Okta, GitLab, Authentik…) with the redirect URL below, and enter the provider URL, client ID and secret.

account.title: My account
account.subtitle: How you sign in to KubeViz.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.hint: Sign in without a password, using this device's fingerprint, face or PIN (or your phone). The passkey stays on the device or in your password manager; KubeViz only stores the public key.
passkeys.name: Passkey name
passkeys.removeHint: It will no longer sign in to KubeViz. The copy on the device can be deleted in its settings.
passkeys.added: Passkey added. Next time, use "Sign in with passkey".
passkeys.exists: This device already has a passkey for this account.
passkeys.unknown: Passkey not recognized. It may have been removed or belong to another KubeViz address.

unsupported.browser: This browser does not support passkeys.
unsupported.ip: Passkeys do not work with an IP address. Open KubeViz by name (e.g. {{host}}).
unsupported.insecure: Passkeys require HTTPS with a trusted certificate (or localhost).

passkeys.hostBound: Passkeys only work on the address where they were created ({{host}}).

metrics.subtitle: What is using CPU and memory: right now (metrics-server) and over time (built-in collector).
metrics.barHint: The bar shows usage over the node's allocatable capacity; the tick marks the total reserved (requests) by pods.

missing.title: The cluster has no metrics-server
missing.body: KubeViz reads CPU and memory usage from the metrics.k8s.io API, provided by metrics-server. To install it:

forbidden.title: Not allowed to read metrics
forbidden.body: Your user cannot read the metrics.k8s.io API. Ask a cluster administrator for read access (get/list on nodes and pods in the metrics.k8s.io group).

error.title: Metrics unavailable
error.body: metrics-server did not respond. It may be starting; the page retries on its own.

metrics.containerBarHint: With a limit, the bar shows usage against it; without one, it is only comparative. The tick marks the request.
metrics.noPods: No pods of this workload right now.

history.title: History
history.empty: No samples in this period yet. The collector samples every {{interval}}.
history.forbidden: You are not allowed to see the history of this scope.

state.missing: No history: the cluster has no metrics-server.
state.forbidden: No history: KubeViz is not allowed to read nodes, pods or metrics. {{error}}
state.error: The metrics collector has an error: {{error}}
state.disabled: Metrics history is disabled in this installation.

history.emptyPrometheus: Prometheus has no data for this scope in this period.
history.podNeedsPrometheus: The history of a single pod requires Prometheus: the built-in collector only keeps the cluster, nodes, namespaces and workloads.

hint.restarts: in the last hour or in CrashLoopBackOff
